analyst_view.overall: Early view: United's situation could look very different by this game, with reports saying the club will decide Michael Carrick's future during the international break, and they visit Liverpool first. Their games have been wild lately, 3-2 against Roma and 4-4 against Villa. Brentford's Igor Thiago is listed as missing after his red card at Brighton; I could not confirm whether his ban runs this long.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean slightly higher: United have scored seven and conceded six in their last two games, and their midfield is without Carlos Baleba for a long spell. United's defending has been the weak point of their season.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, most of them United's. Nothing in the news points either way yet, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. United had only one booking in the 4-4 with Villa, while Brentford collected three cards, including Thiago's red, at Brighton. That evens out, so I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots, 20 of them United's. I lean lower: 20 home shots is a lot for a team in 18th, and Brentford under Keith Andrews are likely to defend and counter. A possible change of manager also adds doubt to how United will play.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. United's recent games have been full of goals, which supports the figure, even if their total shots may come in a little lower. I stay close to the site.
